title: A time average retains at least 87.769 percent of constant-input information in symmetric passive circuit models
abstract: We compared one exact population time average with a full continuous trajectory for a constant input in a symmetric passive stochastic circuit. We assumed known positive definite decay, independent unit white current noise, full observation, and a stationary initial state at the input amplitude. A scalar reduction gives a sharp information fraction of 0.877692222679276 for every duration and input direction. A statistic that adds the two endpoint projections to a weighted time integral retains all path information. We tested 180 point inputs in each of twelve models from two partial adult worm electrical maps, using count and binary weights and three coupling scales. At the primary count scale, the median cell minimum fractions were 0.880172 and 0.879718. Isolated cells attained the scalar bound. Independent covariance and sampled-path calculations checked the formulas. These are model results. They do not establish neural information retention with partial observation, measurement noise, chemical transmission, or an input that starts at recording onset. Original code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction.

display.caption: Time-average information divided by continuous-path information in two adult electrical circuit models. The band spans all 180 point inputs. The dashed line is the proved lower limit under the stated model assumptions.
